sentences.text: 1. The Kengeri Police have charge sheeted the accused for the offences punishable under Sections U/s.498A, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
On 22.07.2014, the complainant and accused marriage was performed and they were living happily together for 2 to 3 years after the marriage and thereafter the accused subjected the complainant to mental and physical cruelty and further the accused on the said date, time and place the accused demanded dowry of Rs.5 Lakhs from the complainant and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty and further on the said date, time and place the accused intentionally insulted the complainant with filthy language with an intention to provoke the complainant to committ the breach of public peace and further on the said date, time and place the accused assaulted the complainant and kicked her and caused simple injuries and further on the said date,
time and place the accused threatened the complainant with dire consequences if she does not bring dowry.
On the first information given by the CW1, FIR came to be registered and after completion of investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for the above said offences.
3. After taking cognizance, this court has complied Section 207 of Cr.P.C. by supplying charge sheet materials to the accused.
The Charges read over and explained to the accused and he has not pleaded guilty of alleged offences and claimed to be tried.

4. The Prosecution in order to prove the case, examined complainant as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to 4.
5.
The 313 Statement of accused dispensed with for having not found any incriminating materials against him.
6. I heard learned APP and learned counsel appearing for the accused.

7. The points that arose for my consideration are:
:: P O I N T S ::
Point No.1 : Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that on 22.07.2014, the complainant and accused marriage was performed and they were living happily together for 2 to 3 years after the marriage and thereafter the accused subjected the complainant to mental and physical cruelty and there by committed offence punishable under section 498A of IPC?
Point No.2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on the said date, time and place the accused accused demanded dowry of Rs.5 Lakhs from the complainant and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty and thereby the accused has committed offence punishable under Snehalatha vs Vishwanath Siddayya Math on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11308038/
2 section 4 of D.P. Act?
Point No.3.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on the said date, time and place the accused intentionally insulted the complainant with filthy language with an intention to provoke the complainant to committ the breach of public peace and thereby the accused has committed offence punishable under section 504 of IPC?
Point No.4.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on the said date, time and place the accused assaulted the complainant and kicked her and caused simple injuries and thereby the accused has committed offence punishable under section 323 of IPC?
Point No.5.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on the said date, time and place the accused threatened the complainant with dire consequences if she does not bring dowry and thereby the accused has committed offence punishable under section 506 of IPC?
Point No.6 : What order?
8. After going through the records and hearing the learned APP and learned counsel for the accused.

I answer the above points as under :
Point No.1 to 5 : In the Negative Point No.6 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 9.
Point No.1 to 5
: As the facts involved in these points are common, in order to avoid repetition of facts, they are taken together for consideration.

10. The prosecution in order to prove its case has examined the complainant as PW1 and got marked complaint at Ex.P1, Panchanama at Ex.P2, marriage photos at Ex.P3 and 4.
11.

The prosecution in order to prove the case has examined the complainant as P.W1 and PW1 in her evidence deposed that, accused is her husband and their marriage was solemnized on 13.02.2014 and they were living in Kengeri and she went to police station with regard to the family dispute and police have taken her signatures in the complaint and panchanama but she does not know the contents of complaint and panchanama and deposed that, the accused has not at all committed any offences against her and she was treated as hostile witness and she was cross-examined by the learned App by suggesting that, the accused has subjected the complainant to mental and physical cruelty demanding dowry and intentionally insulted in filthy language,
assaulted her and threatened with dire consequences if she does not bring dowry.
But all these suggestions were denied by PW1 and nothing worthy was elicited in the course of the cross- examination in favour of the prosecution.

The complainant and accused are wife and husband and complainant herself has not supported the prosecution case and therefore as there are no incriminating materials found against the accused, 313 statement of the accused dispensed with for having not found any incriminating materials against the accused.

Hence accused is entitled for the Snehalatha vs Vishwanath Siddayya Math on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11308038/
3 benefit of doubt and he is entitled to be Acquitted.
Hence, with the above observations, I hold point No.1 to 5 in the NEGATIVE.

12. Point No.6: For the reasons stated and discussion made above, I proceed to pass the following ;
ORDER

The accused is ACQUITTED U/s 248 (1) of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable U/s498A,
323, 504 and 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of D.P. Act.
The bail bonds executed by accused shall be continued for a period of six months.
(Dictated to the stenographer, transcribed and computerized by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 09 th day of October, 2024).
(MANJUNATH D.R.) VI Addl. CJM., Bengaluru City.
